questions.stem: The preservative used if viscera is stored for toxicological examination in autopsy is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Saturated salt solution

Toxicological viscera is preserved in a saturated solution of common salt (sodium chloride).



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 123,124.

questions.stem: Two identical twins will not have same:
questions.solutionHtml:
Fingerprints

Identical twins have the same DNA, but their fingerprints (dactylography) are still different and they do not change.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 86.

Skin, Subcutaneous Fat
  • The clinical entity of degloving injury means that the skin has been lost, but the musculoskeletal unit is intact, and hence, the movements of the part have been preserved.
  • Degloving, also called avulsion, is a type of severe injury that happens when the top layers of your skin and tissue are ripped from the underlying muscle, connective tissue, or bone. It can affect any body part, but it’s more common in the legs
  • Depending on the angle that the tire pulls across the extremity, the skin and subcutaneous tissue may be pulled or sheared off on the leading edge of the extremit



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 191.

questions.stem: In Alleged history of gunshot injury. There is burning, blackening, tattooing around the wound Dirt collar. What is the range?
questions.solutionHtml:
Close shot entry wound
  • Burning, blackening, tattooing around the wound are features of close shot entry.
  • And may occur in contact shots when the muzzle end is not pressed firmly or is loosened by recoil, flame, gas and soot may escape sideways and soil the adjoining skin.
  • Grease collar or dirt collar is seen at firearm entry wounds.
  • It is a black colored ring lining the entrance wound on the skin.
  • It is produced by removal of substances from the bullet as it  grazes through the skin.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 223,226.

questions.stem: Punishment for perjury is under which section IPC ?
questions.solutionHtml:
193 IPC
  • Perjury-the act of telling a lie in a court of law is punishable under S. 193 IPC.
  • Whoever intentionally gives false evidence in any of a judicial proceeding, or fabricates false evidence for the purpose of being used in any stage of a judicial proceeding, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine; and whoever intentionally gives or fabricates false evidence in any other case, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 13.

questions.stem: A child is having Battered baby syndrome how will you identify:
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple Injuries at different ages

Battered child is one which has received repetitive non accidental physical injuries by the parent or guardian .The child will have all types of injuries of all ages.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 445.

Myocardium
  • State of the muscles in a dead body when they become stiff or rigid with some degree of shortening is called Rigor mortis..
  • All muscles of the body are involved i.e. voluntary or involuntary. However, it does not start in all muscles simultaneously (Nysten’s rule).
  • Involuntary muscles (heart) are involved first than voluntary muscles.


KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 160.

questions.stem: Gastric lavage is not contraindicated after ingestion of which acid:
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbolic acid

The only absolute contraindication is corrosive poisoning i.e. alkalis, mineral acid, vegetable acid and organic acids (except carbolic acid).



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 33rd edition, Page number- 534.
